newsitem.title: USA: Conn. governor says new Hartford arena needed.
newsitem.headline: Conn. governor says new Hartford arena needed.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland thinks a new arena is needed to keep the National Hockey League Whalers in Hartford, his press secretary said Friday.
The Whalers have said the state must build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayers' money, if it wants the team to stay.
Rowland met team owner Peter Karmanos Thursday.
The governor previously said he thought a refurbished Civic Center might be a possibility for the Whalers, who say they have lost $33 million over the past two years.

"The governor now agrees with the Whalers that they don't have a long-term future in Hartford by staying at the Civic Center," Rowland's press secretary Dean Pagani told Reuters. "He's agreed to study whether it makes sense to build a new facility for the team."
Rowland will review the study's findings in about a month, said Pagani.
Pagani said the two sides were not necessarily far apart. "Both the governor and the Whalers want the team to stay in Hartford," he said.
"The question is what (Rowland) can support as the representative of all the taxpayers. Is it in the best interests of the state of Connecticut to make another large investment in the Whalers?"
Rowland has said he wants a solution that would guarantee keeping the Whalers in Hartford for 20 or 30 years.
The team's Civic Center lease expires after the 1997-98 season.
Karmanos has said he cannot sustain the same kind of losses the team has suffered for the past two years.
The meeting on Thursday was the first between the governor and the team owner in three months.
